title: Students and teachers call nationwide strikes and rallies over university funding

tea.why: Protesters argue that government funding and recruitment plans for universities are insufficient after years of austerity.
tea.want: They demand 150,000 new university places, increased funding, higher wages, and the repeal of Parcoursup and Mon Master systems.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Authorities approved a protest route in Paris from Place de la Bastille to the Panthéon for November 26.

summary: An inter-union coalition of students and higher education staff has called for a nationwide day of strikes and rallies on November 26, 2026. This action follows two months of ongoing protests. Organisers, including FSU, Unsa, CGT, SUD, FO, Unef, and others, state that recent government announcements regarding 20,000 additional university places are inadequate. They demand 150,000 new places, increased public funding, and the repeal of the Parcoursup and Mon Master systems. In Paris, a march is scheduled to begin at 14:00 at Place de la Bastille and conclude at the Panthéon. The route has been approved by the police prefecture. Additionally, police unions have called for separate gatherings at police stations on the same day to present an ultimatum to the government regarding their own working conditions.
demands: Repeal of Parcoursup and Mon Master
Increased funding for universities and laboratories
Higher wages for staff and student grants
response: The government previously announced the creation of 20,000 additional places, the future evolution of Parcoursup by 2027, and the indexation of student grants to inflation.

updates.text: An inter-union coalition announced a new day of mobilization for November 26.
The Paris police prefecture approved the march route from Place de la Bastille to the Panthéon.
